target_customer: vehicle owners (consumers, employer-benefit members, rideshare/rental hosts) and fleets paying for on-site fueling, maintenance and inspections
problem: Fueling and servicing a car means detours to gas stations and shops; Yoshi brings fuel and car care to the vehicle's location.
business_model: membership/subscription plus per-service fees (gas delivery launched at $20/month in San Francisco); later employer-benefit and B2B partnerships
product_category: mobile fuel delivery and on-site car care (later EV charging, virtual inspections)

founders.name: Dan Hunter
founders.background_notes: Listed as Daniel Hunter in some coverage.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling and dispatch software plus fueling operations; the difficulty is operational (safety, permits, logistics) rather than technical.

defensibility.rationale: Several competitors (Filld, WeFuel, Mobile Fuel, Purple, Booster, Wrench) did the same service in 2016-17; strategic backers (GM Ventures, ExxonMobil) and partnerships were the main edge, which came later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy it; GM Ventures and ExxonMobil instead invested. Yoshi remained independent through its April 2024 Series C.

market_need_then: Founders cited fuel and maintenance as more than doubling lifetime cost of ownership (YC page) and a gas-station model unchanged since 1910; early launch coverage showed paying subscribers at $20/month in San Francisco.

pivots.from: gas delivery subscription in San Francisco
pivots.to: broader mobile car care (fuel plus washing and services), expanding to new cities
pivots.why: per TechCrunch the 2017 seed was to fill up or wash cars anywhere and expand to new towns; later added preventative maintenance, virtual inspections and EV charging (2024).

outcome_analysis: Yoshi started as a $20-per-month gas delivery service in San Francisco, raised a small seed in 2017 and then GM- and ExxonMobil-backed rounds, and broadened into maintenance, virtual inspections, employer benefits and EV charging, reaching a $26M Series C in April 2024 with total funding near $65M. It is still operating with about 125 staff, helped by strategic corporate backers and partnerships such as Uber and Turo, though absolute revenue is not disclosed.
notes: Series A/B amounts and investors are from aggregator pages and search summaries (seedtable, altair.vc repost); they sum with the others to about $64.9M, matching CB Insights' $64.92M total, hence coverage 'complete'. Founding year conflict: YC page says 2015, EV Report says 2016. Series C valuation: a search summary of TechCrunch says $200M+, the EV Report says undisclosed, so post_money left null. Preqin dates Series C to June 2023; most say April 2024. Headquarters: Nashville per YC, San Francisco per Dealroom. Founder bios not found. 2016 seed ($120K) was stated in launch coverage, not a priced round.
